message.content:
Methane, **CH\(_4\)**, has **four identical covalent C–H single bonds**.[1][3] In the common valence-bond description, carbon uses **sp\(^3\)** hybrid orbitals, giving methane a **tetrahedral** shape with bond angles of about **109.5°**; each C–H bond is a **sigma bond** formed by end-to-end orbital overlap.[1][2]

If you want, I can also explain the **Lewis structure**, **hybridization**, or **bond polarity** of methane.
